https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/.text: Military Menu Introduction Systems Facilities Agencies Industry Operations Countries Hot Documents News Reports Policy Budget Congress Links WMD Intelligence Homeland Security Space Military Estonian and Latvian foreign ministry directorates discuss bilateral cooperation and regional security Republic of Estonia - Ministry of Foreign Affairs 04.09.2026 | 13:15 On 3-4 September, Undersecretary for Political Affairs Martin Roger took part in a seminar bringing together the leaderships of the Estonian and Latvian foreign ministries. The discussions focused on bilateral cooperation, shared foreign policy objectives and regional security. According to Roger, Estonia and Latvia, as close neighbours and Allies, are united by common interests and goals. Estonia and Latvia stand firmly with Ukraine, work to increase the cost of Russia's aggression, and are strengthening regional security together. In the current security environment, close cooperation between the two countries and a united voice in Europe are more important than ever. Cooperation between Estonia and Latvia is close and wide-ranging, extending from security and defence to the economy and cross-border cooperation. During the seminar, the leaderships of the two foreign ministries visited the 2nd Infantry Brigade at Kuperjanov Barracks, where representatives of the Kuperjanov Infantry Battalion gave them an overview of the unit's activities and tasks. The joint seminar of the Estonian and Latvian foreign ministry directorates was held for the eleventh time.

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cme3.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma in Okinawa, Japan By Sakshi Venkatraman Published 1 hour ago A US Marine has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a woman's body was found in a hotel in Okinawa, Japan, local officials say. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described the crime as a "brutal and heinous" robbery and murder. She said she had urged the US to "enforce stricter discipline" of its personnel. Japan's public broadcaster NHK identified the victim as Yagi Anna, 39, and the suspect as Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who is stationed at US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma. "We are actively cooperating with Japanese authorities, in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine," the Marine Corps said on social media, extending condolences to the victim's family. Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said the woman's body was discovered early Saturday morning in a hotel in Naha City, the capital of the Okinawa prefecture. "Such an incident is utterly inexcusable and fills me with strong indignation," Koizumi wrote on social media, adding that "incidents and accidents involving U.S. military personnel cause significant anxiety to the local community and must never occur". The US Embassy in Tokyo said that it was fully cooperating with the Japanese government and local police. Japan's foreign ministry said it summoned US ambassador George Glass to discuss the incident on Sunday. Okinawa is home to several US military bases and tens of thousands of American troops. Okinawa Governor Genta Koja says the prefecture has repeatedly demanded that the US take action to prevent such incidents, and said he sees the alleged crime as a sign of a lack of discipline. "The fact that this kind of event has happened again leaves us no choice but to conclude that the US military's efforts in maintaining discipline, educating personnel, and other such measures are completely ineffective," he said. https://english.republika.mk/macedonia/f.text: A government delegation led by Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski is currently in the United States, where, among other engagements, they attended the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Following yesterday’s session, Mickoski noted the focus of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly—attended by world leaders—on revitalizing global cooperation, providing a crucial boost to the Sustainable Development Goals, and fostering collective action for peace, dignity, and equality on a healthy planet. The delegation is also scheduled to participate today in a meeting of European Union and Western Balkans leaders, reported the MIA special correspondent from New York. The meeting is being chaired by Kaja Kallas, the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy. Ahead of the meeting, Macedonian Prime Minister Mickoski called for the involvement of EU representatives to help improve the dialogue regarding differences with Bulgaria Prime Minister Mickoski also reported that positive signals are emerging from the European Union, particularly following the EU-Western Balkans summit in Tivat, which saw the launch of an initiative by Germany and France to reform the enlargement process.
